title: Bio Lesson Notes
subject: Biology
content:
HUMAN DIGESTIVE SYSTEM
Is a system involved in the breakdown of ingested food into smaller molecules that can be absorbed into the  blood stream and eventually the body cells and tissues.
This process takes place in the alimentary canal or gut
Food substances are broken down in the alimentary canal or  gut.
Examples of food substances are: carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, lipids and mineral salts.
PARTS OF THE  HUMAN DIGESTIVE SYSTEM

DIGESTION
Is the breaking down of food into smaller molecules that can be absorbed by the body.

TYPES OF DIGESTION
* Physical
* Chemical
PHYSICAL DIGESTION
Is the process whereby food is broken down into smaller particles exerting an external force onto the food.
This only changes the form of food
CHEMICAL DIGESTION
Is the breaking down of food particles into smaller molecules using enzymes.
This changes the food materials from simple to complex.

DIGESTION IN THE MOUTH
In the mouth, teeth grinds food making it swallow-able hence  increasing the surface area for enzymes
The tongue has taste buds which makes us perceive the flavour of the food,
The tongue also mixes the food with saliva. 
Saliva is produced by salivary glands.
Saliva moistens the food.

Salivary Glands
Produce saliva which  contain water, mucus, salivary amylase. 
Water softens the food.
Mucus makes food slippery for easy swallowing.
Salivary amylase digest starch to maltose.
Epiglottis
Is a piece of tissue that covers  the entrance into the trachea when swallowing.
Epiglottis stops the food particles from entering into the wind pipe.
Oesophagus: moves the food down  to the stomach in a process called swallowing.

Stomach
Carries out mechanical/physical digestion. 
Due to its muscular contractions food is mixed with mucus and enzymes forming chime.
It carries out chemical digestion, since its walls produce enzymes that digest the food.
The Small Intestine
Has two parts 
1. the duodenum
2. the ileum 
Duodenum
Is the first part of  the small intestines.
Has two organs
* Pancreas
* Liver
Pancreas and gall bladder secrete juices into this part. 
Pancreasproduce pancreatic juice onto the food and gall bladder secrete bile onto the food passing in this part.
Liver
Secretes bile which is stored by the gall bladder. 
The gall bladder secretes bile into the duodenum via a bile duct. 
Bile emulsifies fats.
It also neutralise acidic chyme.
Pancreas: produce pancreatic juice which contains amylase-digests starch into maltose. Trypsin-digests proteins into amino acids
Ileum
Is the second part of the small intestine.
Functions
1. completely break down of food
2. absorption of digested food.
Large intestine(COLON):
receives the residues of digestion mostly cellulose. 
Function
1. to absorb large volumes of water and salt. 
2. to synthesize vitamin K.
Rectum
Stores the  undigestible food temporarily before being passed out as faeces through a process called defaecation.
Appendix
no function in humans
Anus: Is the outlet for faeces
